JUST IN: The entire petrochemical arc of the Persian Gulf is on fire, offline, or suspended. Count the countries. Iran: 85 percent of petrochemical production destroyed by Israeli strikes on Asaluyeh and Mahshahr. Qatar: two LNG trains and 17 percent of export capacity offline for three to five years after Iranian missiles hit Ras Laffan. UAE: Borouge polyolefin plant suspended, Habshan gas complex shut with 80 percent of domestic gas supply offline, Asab degassing station burning since March 29th, Bu Hasa oil field hit. Saudi Arabia: fires at Jubail Industrial City after Iranian missiles struck the SABIC petrochemical hub, one of the largest integrated chemical complexes on earth. Kuwait: airport fuel tanks ablaze, two power and desalination units offline, Oil Ministry facilities hit, 15 American servicemembers injured at Ali Al Salem air base. Bahrain: GPIC petrochemical units attacked, BAPCO storage tank fire. Six countries. One war. Every major energy producer on the Persian Gulf has taken damage.

The global numbers are now quantifiable. C&EN reports 12 percent of global ethylene capacity is offline. The Dow CEO told Fortune that approximately 20 percent of global petrochemical capacity is blocked by the Hormuz closure and strikes combined. The Middle East operates 193 petrochemical complexes supplying 22 percent of global output. The GCC alone accounts for 12 percent, or 150 million tonnes per year. Asia’s naphtha feedstock supply has been throttled by 7 to 8 million tonnes. S&P Global estimates 10 to 11 million tonnes of paraxylene production lost. These are not projections. They are current measurements of capacity that is not producing.

The war did not discriminate. Israel struck Iran’s plants to deny IRGC revenue and missile chemistry. Iran struck Gulf plants to impose symmetric pain on the countries hosting American forces and benefiting from the scarcity premium. The UAE’s damage came from the debris of its own successful interceptions falling onto the facilities the interceptors were protecting. Kuwait’s power and desalination plants were hit by Iranian drones while 15 American troops at Ali Al Salem took shrapnel from another. Saudi Arabia’s Jubail, which produces methanol, ethylene glycol, and fertiliser feedstocks for global markets, burned overnight. The fires in Bahrain’s BAPCO storage were extinguished. The fires in Jubail had not been when this was written.

The molecule does not care about the flag over the facility. Polyethylene from Borouge and polyethylene from Asaluyeh and polyethylene from Jubail all serve the same Asian markets. All three sources are now offline or suspended. The syringe wrapper in Dhaka, the water pipe in Jakarta, the food container in Manila, the fertiliser pellet in Lahore, all of them originate in the Persian Gulf’s petrochemical arc, and the arc is dark from Asaluyeh to Jubail to Ras Laffan to Ruwais to Shuaiba.

Hegseth said the most recent overnight strikes on Iran are the largest since day one. Tomorrow will be bigger. Iran’s response has been to hit every Gulf nation hosting American assets or profiting from the war. The reciprocal destruction is not collateral. It is doctrine. Israel degrades Iran’s chemistry. Iran degrades the Gulf’s processing. Both sides lose capacity. Asia loses supply. And the 12 to 20 percent of global petrochemical output that is now offline will not return until the war ends, the mines are cleared, the heat exchangers are manufactured, and the utilities are rebuilt. That timeline is not weeks. It is years. And Tuesday is today. Europe markets might open in to a bloodbath.

$GRAB Strong Liquidity is Winning! 🧵
TLDR: $GRAB MTUs could reach 120-140m MTUs by 2027. Read more below

2024-2025, most shareholders criticized $GRAB management for having way too much Cash on Balance sheet, without understanding $GRAB wants GrabFin to be a major % of overall business, similar to Wechat. 

Gross cash liquidity stood at approximately $7.4 billion (including cash, short-term/long-term deposits, marketable securities, and restricted cash)

This is a robust war chest  is currently playing strongly in its favor for both consolidation opportunities in Southeast Asia (SEA) and pursuing acquisitions at attractive prices. Here's a clear breakdown based on the latest financials and strategic moves as of early 2026.

The business now requires relatively low capex in its core mobility and delivery segments, allowing it to sustain or grow this cushion while funding growth. Management has highlighted this liquidity as providing "greater flexibility to accelerate our platform ambitions" while also authorizing a $500 million share repurchase program (partly executed via accelerated share repurchase). 

A prime Example was in Late March, where GRAB paid for Foodpanda at the price that is less than 2 P/S, and opening up 23m people TAM in Taiwan, 2nd highest income after Singapore. Foodpanda Taiwan is already profitable with operations in 21 cities and meaningful GMV.

A big cash pile means Grab can execute such deals without needing to raise capital, dilute shareholders, or take on heavy debt especially useful in a higher-interest-rate environment or when regulators scrutinize leveraged deals. The Taiwan move also shows Grab can deploy capital opportunistically (note: Uber's prior attempt to buy foodpanda Taiwan was blocked by regulators, creating an opening for Grab at what appears a reasonable price). 

The next most anticipated acquisition will probably be $GOTO Mobility/Delivery, where this could send GRAB Indonesia market share to 95%+. It would add 30-40m MTUs or more, 3-4m drivers and millions of merchants overnight. Some sources cited $GOTO has much larger user number, but I just don't buy it, so I want to keep it in the 30-40m MTUs. 

$GOTO Mobility/Delivery segment with FoodPanda Taiwan would add roughly 45m-50m MTUs to $GRAB or bring total to 100m+ MTUs=> Consolidation!

Some sources already indicated $GOTO may be acquired at a very reasonable price like FoodPanda Taiwan, or for $755–765 million revenue, that would be $750m-$1B+. Which is a very welcoming new if true.  

In 2025, I said FoodPanda is losing market share to $GRAB in Singapore, Malaysia and Philippines. They have to service debt or reduce it somehow. This will most likely end in FoodPanda exiting these 3 markets like they did in Thailand (May 2025). 

Essentially, once all consolidated, $GRAB would likely to have 120-140m MTUs. Rising interest rate and fuel price are pushing this to a beautiful and happy ending, which I did not anticipate in 2025, but here we are back to global QT. This will certainly invite some new players coming in, and more reasons to push even more "affordable" products to maintain "Monopoly" legally. 

GrabFin should generate FCF and profitability by H2 2026, or from Q3 2026, we should see Grab generating $1-$1.5B adjusted FCF TTM pre-consolidation, or $2B+ after $GOTO Mobility/Delivery + FoodPanda exit in 3 Markets or sell to $GRAB for $500m. 

More FCF will mean more expansion, faster MTUs growth toward my full thesis 350-400m, and higher conversion to DTUs, which the group spend much more frequently. I'm excited for 2027 already!!!!!

$GRAB Stash Acquisition is a Long-Term Play🧵

1. CFO comment:
Why did we do Stash? It's really a unique asset. If you look at the trend of when we do acquisitions, if you looked at the last unique asset that we acquired was around supermarkets, the Giant and Everrise. We see Stash as a very unique asset with a few things. One is, it's got a very strong IP, and it's got a strong talent pool and a platform that we don't have today.

If you look at financial services as a business, what do we have? We have a very strong payments. We have a strong lending business, which is continuing to scale. We have a big deposit base of 7 million customers on the deposit side, with on the banking side of the house. What's missing? We don't have an investing platform today, and that's really critical for us as we continue to fill, complete the full picture of financial services in Southeast Asia, also in other parts of the market where Stash operates today. Now, it is a positive EBITDA business today. It is generating free cash flow positive, and we see this business generating $60 million in EBITDA in 2028. So it's an accretive business that we see.

But really, it's important that we also serve our user base today, not only in extending loans, but also teaching them how to save. It's critical in terms of our mission for the underserved, especially on financial services. So we're very excited to have the Stash family joining us. So we expect to close this transaction sometime in Q3 or Q4. They're a great team. We already have over a million customers that we're looking to serve, that they have continued to prove that their product works. And as they continue to build their product set out, we're then going to continue to penetrate the U.S. market. But also, over time, we'll introduce the product here in Southeast Asia.

2. Stash acquisition and the Foodpanda Taiwan deal do point to a dual-track strategy for Grab disciplined international expansion paired with deeper monetization and organic growth in its core Southeast Asia (SEA) ecosystem, including financial services like an investing platform.

This suggests Grab is expanding selectively and opportunistically by leveraging acquisitions of established, profitable delivery operations rather than building from scratch. This shows willingness to step outside pure SEA while staying in familiar high-density Asian markets, like I talked about in 2025. 

The ambition is clearly global, and $GRAB Long shareholders with high conviction shall have the highest ROI. As Grab generates more FCF, they will expand more and help those folks to invest in the best stock market in the world( The U.S.)

3. There is no investing/wealth management product live for SEA users today, and Grab wants to fill that GAP for 5 billion people surviving and thriving at th bottom of the pyramid. 

~Stash already enables US stock/ETF investing for its users, so the technology, compliance framework (for US assets), and product design exist.
~Grab sees cross-border opportunities between Stash’s platform and its 50.5+ million monthly transacting users in SEA.
~Many SEA users (especially in Singapore, which has sophisticated retail investors) show interest in international diversification, including US tech stocks and ETFs. This is a game changer for people to "buy US stocks through the Grab platform."

Investing in US stocks requires compliance with US securities laws (for US assets) plus local SEA regulations in each country. My best estimate is early 2027 in certain countries and expand to the rest long term. 

SEA's retail investing scene has expanded rapidly in recent years, driven by rising middle-class wealth, smartphone penetration, digital trading apps, and a young population. US stocks appeal and perceived higher returns, but barriers like currency risk, regulations, taxes, and limited local platform access keep participation selective.

Singapore: Highest interest. Sophisticated retail base with easy access via brokers. Policies boosting local market liquidity also indirectly support overall investing confidence, including global diversification.

Indonesia & Vietnam: Strong retail stock culture (millions of new accounts), but mostly local. Some high-net-worth or urban youth explore US via apps, especially for tech exposure.

Malaysia, Thailand, Philippines: Moderately strong. Growing digital investing, but domestic markets and regional plays dominate. Young investors want to invest in US stocks, but lacking a platform.
